content.title: About
content.content: Canned turkey is a ready‑to‑eat product made from turkey meat that is cooked, sliced and sealed in airtight cans with salt, spices and sometimes a small amount of fat. It can be stored at room temperature for several years.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned turkey is a staple in military rations and backpacking meals because of its long shelf life.
In the United States, “turkey breast” cans are popular for their easy‑to‑slice, boneless meat.
The canning process kills most bacteria while preserving most of the protein and B‑vitamins.
Some varieties are packed with a light broth or sauce to enhance flavor.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Canned turkey provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many meat cans, turkey has moderate fat content, making it suitable for lower‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals help the immune system and blood formation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B3 and B6 aid metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain high levels of salt; people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to bird meat.

items.title: BPA in packaging
items.content: Metal cans can be lined with BPA‑containing coatings; choose products from reputable brands.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned turkey can be eaten straight from the can, added to salads, sandwiches, pastas, or used in hot dishes such as stews, casseroles and omelets.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer the meat to an airtight container and keep it in the refrigerator, consuming within 3–4 days.
